children: Kalpana Pathak Mumbai: Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) is set to significantly reduce its Russian crude oil purchases in November as higher freight costs and elevated premiums make Middle Eastern grades more commercially attractive, signalling a shift in the state-run refiner's sourcing strategy.

Russian crude accounted for around 37% of BPCL's crude sourcing mix in the July-September quarter. However, the company has cut purchases of Russian cargoes for the month of November as shipping costs have risen, Vetsa Ramakrishna Gupta, BPCL's head of finance, said on Monday. "October, our requirement from Russia has slightly come down, but in November, cargoes from Russia have reduced significantly due to their commercial viability. Mainly due to the increase in freight, we are not getting good offers from Russia," Gupta told analysts on a call.

The company expects supplies from the Middle East to increase in October and November compared with the first quarter, when disruptions to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz affected supplies from the region. "October-November also, we are expecting similar lengths of higher volume from the Middle East.

Mainly after the Yanbu pipeline correction by Saudi, they have started increasing their volumes," Gupta said, adding that supplies from Iraq and Kuwait had yet to return to full levels, while volumes from the rest of the Middle East were healthy. The shift comes amid a broader trend among Indian refiners to reduce purchases of Russian crude when competing grades from the Middle East offer better economics.

The premium on Russian oil for December cargoes has fallen to $1-2 per barrel over regional benchmarks, compared with $12-13 per barrel for October cargoes, Gupta said. BPCL also expects its refinery runs to moderate in the third and fourth quarters of the current financial year as it undertakes planned maintenance at its facilities.

Some units at the company's Mumbai refinery will undergo a scheduled shutdown lasting around 30 days. At its Kochi refinery, certain units will undergo maintenance turnarounds lasting 30-40 days. Separately, BPCL plans to dilute at least a 30% stake in its proposed refinery and petrochemicals project in Andhra Pradesh, indicating its intention to bring in an investment partner for the project.

title: BPCL to Cut Russian Oil Buying as West Asian Crude Gains Edge
